_spec.purpose: The variety engine. No two decks visually alike.
_spec.why: Each run records the techniques, palette, structure and camera it used, and the next run reads this to know what it may not reach for again. Without it a machine converges on whatever worked once, which is how a daily product develops a house style nobody chose.
_spec.enforced_by: scripts/carousel/bespoke_check.py measures WITHIN a deck. This ledger constrains ACROSS decks. Both are needed: a deck can be nine different drawings that all look like last Tuesday.

entries.renumbered_after_the_cut: Recorded at the third scoring pass. The register, three palette notes and the camera line were all written against the nine slide plan and survived the cut of slide 4 unchanged, so this entry named the wrong frame for the paper inversion, for both accent fills and in every camera move after the fourth. entries.bespoke_measurement_note: 0.5314 was this deck's first measurement and it was wrong about the deck, not about the gate's arithmetic. bespoke_check was still counting the standing masthead, which this run put on every frame: on the closest pair it shared 50 tokens and exactly one was a drawing call. The gate now strips anything carrying a tx- class. RE-MEASURED under the corrected gate, the two earlier decks move only 0.3997 to 0.4061 and 0.2298 to 0.2300, because neither carried that masthead. Their own entries keep the figures they shipped with, which is what those runs were judged on.
entries.rebuilt_at_the_ninth_pass: Three techniques in this list named frames that were replaced during scoring and were caught by two judges reading the ledger against the renders. Slide 7 was recorded as a redaction field of struck bars, which is a drawing nobody made: two judges read the struck bars as an assertion that something had been struck out, which c17 does not support, and it was rebuilt as the survey title block its own dossier had asked for. Slide 3 was recorded as a flat field of identical cells and was rebuilt under one raking key, because a flat frame reads as an unfinished render and its own risks list said so. Slide 6 ran its courses DOWN, which forced four display words to 90 degrees under four near-black plates, and now runs them across. The ledger is the next run's only memory of what not to reuse, so a technique recorded here that never shipped blocks tomorrow from a drawing nobody made and leaves the drawing that ran unrecorded. This entry is now written against the renders rather than against the plan.

November 3rd is DENIED the red on every frame it appears on, because a nonbinding election is not a deadline and the deck's argument is that the date which looks like the decision is not the one. Measured 5.12 to 1 on the stock and 2.89 on the dark ground, which is why only a paper frame could carry it.

The county map went after panel two, which found it asserting a county membership no claim supports and a universal negative that is probably wrong. structural_laws: every mark is either printed or added, never both, and a press artifact is a third thing. Slide 2's second impression of the opening clause is letterforms and is nobody's line to read, declared aria-hidden and decorative at a measured 1.47 to 1

the two GROUNDS never mix, and lit paper is not a ground. A frame stands on stock or on houston_black and never both. Stock VALUE appears on three of the dark frames, on the charter's lit course, the ballot card and the bounded figure, because paper under the deck's one lamp reads as paper wherever it lies. The law as first written said stock never crosses at all, and the fourth panel was right that the renders had already contradicted it
the palette is craft and never evidence, so no frame names a soil

the perforation never tears, because the election has not happened
the stock is new, no stains, no yellowing, no deckle
no numeral appears that is not in claims.json, and no county and no distance appears at all

entries.register: a Texas road at night in returned light, with one noon inversion. Retroreflective return is the deck's physical law and it carries the argument for free: a mark returns light when the record holds it, and the one mount that carries nothing returns nothing
techniques: an axonometric instrument authored directly in SVG, mounted on a roof plane with thickness through a drawn pedestal casting an occlusion shadow on the sheet metal
a broken time scale, two lanes both linear in elapsed days at different rates, with a filled wedge whose top edge spans exactly the segment the lower lane redraws
a lit caliche haze band with the rig standing in it in silhouette, the air lit rather than the vehicle
an SVG tally of 1,400 marks in 280 groups of five, asserted at build time, under one emitter falloff computed per group index
four parallax planes and a crossing in pure CSS with no raster context on the frame at all
a single class county choropleth through TXGeo's Albers, lit on the seams by a raking sodium lamp so 254 identical fills do not read as a bed
a one point perspective road with the centre line's dashes placed by GROUND DISTANCE and projected, and retroreflective return kept as a separate term from diffuse ambient

a glyph mask driving corduroy striations INSIDE the letterforms with a lit offset edge, on pavement that stayed unmilled. WHAT SHIPPED, not what was planned. The plan was a milled band with the shadow on the near wall and the light on the far one so the type read as cut into the shoulder, and the sixth panel's craft judge measured the pavement behind the glyphs at the same value as the shoulder above and below it, so there is no band and no trough. The type reads as raised on the road rather than cut into it, which is the inverse of the technique, and the offset edge reads as misregistration. This line said the planned thing until that judge read the render and found the ledger had recorded a drawing nobody made, which is the one failure this file exists to make impossible
an SVG guide sign panel with its plate measured from the laid out legend

Two frames were REBUILT from the ground up after the pixel critics, slide 2 because a hook promising seven marks showed six at feed size, and slide 7 because its haze wedge had its apex on its own subject and its three stripes were painted out at full opacity by two band wells the frame drew over itself.
structural_laws: returned light means the record holds it. The one mount carrying no date returns nothing and takes one rim of the lamp, and it is the darkest area in its lane
no numeral is typed. The first panel found three that were, on three frames, and each one is now interpolated from the code that computes it

no coordinate is printed. Three shipped in the first render and two of the three were wrong against the gazetteer's own computed centroids

every word on a frame is DOM text, and this deck BROKE IT on slide 8. A date on a chart is copy, and canvas fillText ships it as a bitmap that copy_sync, the vector PDF and a screen reader all miss. Slide 2's twelve raster labels were moved to the DOM when the first panel found them, and slide 8's four header strings were not, so the one frame whose entire subject is a machine readable header row ships that row as four bitmaps. machine_qa warns about it four times in the same file this entry says it was written from, and the law sat here stated and broken for three panels before the seventh read the warnings against the law and said so
a container's edge is not its content's edge. Three frames shipped a paragraph, a stripe or a tally row cut by a plate before this was written down

entries.register: a Texas notice case seen nine ways, wide range about a median of 52.1. Anodized rail, dark case interior and cream bond carry through six of the nine frames as one object under changing light and camera. Measured against the mid value deck its own storyboard declared, one of the nine sits inside the L* 62 to 68 band that plan set, and the frames run 14.4 to 93.2.
techniques: a wall mounted notice case authored as geometry so every overlay knows where it is, with a keyway and hinge knuckles so it reads as locked
a cast occlusion shadow whose penumbra widens with the air gap, the deck's one depth cue

per row cast shadows that LENGTHEN AND SOFTEN together down the board, a short crisp contact core plus a body that loses density and gains penumbra with distance from one overhead source, at a step the frame's own script asserts clears three device pixels between neighbours
true one point perspective shared by a canvas projection and a CSS transform on the type, so the case and the words on it are one object
additive veiling glare drawn ABOVE the type as a screening layer, so a reflection lifts ink and paper together and contrast collapses

a bounded specular blowout at 28 degrees with a computed shoulder, running the whole of a FULL BLEED page with no border, its lower shoulder grading into the frame's only dark, which is a surface rather than an edge
repetition down a computed cosine bounce falloff, four identical minute lines brightening 16.5 L* from first to last
a sheared and rippled Fresnel weighted mirror resolving a second notice case, carrying nothing legible

two slips HUNG from the clips that held nothing for eight frames, each shrink wrapped to its own longest laid out line and hung from its own margin above the case lip, so no width and no top on that frame is typed

fiberboard cork as a fine 2px speckle over a lit gradient on frames 6 and 9, with a low frequency mottle over it on frame 6 ONLY, because the grain alone is right at 2160 and gone by 432 and frame 6 is the frame whose whole field is cork

a felt letterboard seating five rows of WORDS, each in a two part groove whose dark channel crosses the glyph baseline so the letters occlude the slot they stand in, with two characters set proud by content rather than by index. The board carries no tiles, no months and no numerals. The earlier entry recorded all three
brass pins whose shafts go THROUGH the paper, so the cast shadow falls on the card and not on the cork

three route slips whose paper is measured from the type laid out inside them, at widths the frame's own script refuses within 12 percent of each other, over a staple field whose exclusion is read off getBoundingClientRect and which RESAMPLES rather than skips so it does not thin out wherever the type is

a reflected notice case carrying the near case's own vocabulary at half contrast, a lit top rail, two stiles at two values, a lower rail and a keyway, run through the same shear and ripple so it belongs to the pane

The classes, counted off this list and nothing else: near frontal on a locked case (1), square on to a bordered sheet (2 and 7), a felt letterboard square on and level (3), steep oblique in true perspective (4), a full bleed crop with no case and no border (5), level on a flat field with no case (6), a shaded case with a reflected second case in it (8), a close crop with two ground planes and hung paper (9).

value.counted_by: out/2026-08-25/tmp/write_measured.py, over the array above. entries.cut: nothing was cut. Frame 2 went from seven instruments in one column to FIFTEEN in two when the set became a computed selection over the record, and its greeked filler field went with them, because a sheet with fifteen real lines on it does not need filler pretending to be lines. Frame 3 stayed a ROSTER and stopped being a bar chart of blank tiles: it seats five rows of WORDS in two part grooves whose dark channel crosses the glyph baseline, with two characters proud. It carries no tiles, no months and no numerals, and an earlier draft of this field said it carried all three, one field away from the technique line that says it does not. Frame 4 stopped being a third Fort Worth frame and became the sentence the deck proves and never said, that not one of the five resolutions is among the five that took effect. Frame 5 lost its border. Frame 9 was rebuilt from a hearing date with no door into the two dated public steps this record's data center items still carry.
entries.structural_laws: nothing carved, embossed, milled or engraved anywhere. All depth from the air gap between glazing and sheet. No raking key. No cartography and no coordinate. No invented item number, party name or building.
entries.avoid_next: the notice case itself for at least one cycle, and any deck that declares a value band without measuring it. The square on bordered sheet is down to two frames this run, from four, so it is no longer the thing to avoid, but a third would be. This field and `camera` above are composed from ONE list of frames, because round 5 found them disagreeing, five against four, inside the entry whose own note says every number in it comes from one source.
entries.palette_note: edge_cyan is GONE from this deck. It shipped as a 6px bar at x16 on frame 6, attached to no drawn object, unterminated at both ends, 2.4px wide at the size a reader gets, through three craft reads. A reserved colour that buys nothing is deleted rather than elaborated.

entries.light_decks_used: MEASURED, AND THIS DECK BREACHES THE CAP ON THE OWNER'S WAIVER. brand.yaml allows a light deck at most once per eight runs and says the ledger enforces the count. It did not: every light_decks_used value in this file read the literal 1 while meaning light FRAMES inside a deck, a different quantity from the one brand.yaml says is counted. Measured off the shipped PNGs on 2026-08-26: 08-18 at deck median L* 82.7, 08-20 at 85.5 and this deck at 86.7, three light decks in an eight run window against a cap of one, and two of the three had already shipped before anyone counted. A reader judge asserted it as a hard fail and was right. Waived by the owner for this deck. ledger_check.check_register now counts it off value.deck_median_L rather than off anything a run writes about itself, so the cap binds from here.

value.arc_note: THE PLANNED TURN DID NOT SHIP AS THE BRIGHTEST FRAME. The storyboard puts the turn on the deck's lightest frame and slide 6 measures 70.6 against slide 5 at 91.4. The per frame acceptance passed because it asks only that the span be the lightest region ON ITS OWN FRAME, so nothing caught the arc level miss.

entries.cut: nothing cut. Slide 5 was rebuilt twice, first off the technology vocabulary that duplicated slide 7 and onto the repayment stake, then from seated plates to incised ones when three judges still read 5 and 7 as one picture. Pixel correlation between that pair went from the closest in the deck to -0.03.
entries.structural_laws: ONE SUN at azimuth 246 degrees on every frame, one cast length of 2.75x apparent height, contact at the foot rather than a drop shadow. A built thing casts and an unbuilt thing does not, posed on slide 2 and answered on slide 3. No sixteen marks on slide 6: the record holds the COUNT of pages carrying the words and not their folios.
entries.avoid_next: the raking daylight limestone register for at least one cycle, and any ground tooth written as a single noise layer. This run found every tooth loop in the deck thresholding a -1..1 fbm2 signal as if it returned 0..1, firing the dark fleck on 0.6 percent of cells and the light one on 87.8, and running at a feature size near 400px. Both are fixed and both would have shipped again.

entries.cut: nothing was cut. Slide 5 was rebuilt twice, first because the knockout composited in the wrong order and the backlit cuts rendered as dark embossed type, then again because the letterforms shipped as canvas raster and the deck's single most important sentence would have reached the platform as a bitmap. It is SVG text over the canvas walls now, with the overlap declared. ROUND FOUR, ON FRAME 5, RECORDED BECAUSE A JUDGE ASKED FOR IT AND WAS RIGHT TO. The cut is built as two feOffset copies of the glyph alpha, dark at minus six and light at plus six, under a gradient fill. Round three and round four both read the result as an emboss rather than an aperture, and round four named the cost precisely: the lit rim falls in the opposite quadrant to this deck's own lamp, which sits upper left on frames 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8, and law 3 of this deck forbids anything embossed. THE FRAME SHIPS THAT WAY. It is recorded here as a MISS rather than described as met, the same way frame 9's stencil is, because the run corrected the frame 9 ledger line after a judge caught it and would otherwise have left its twin standing three frames earlier. The rebuild the craft lens asked for, feDiffuseLighting over a blurred alpha lit at the deck's own azimuth, is a proposal in the run record.

panel_repairs: FRAME 4 PRINTED A JOIN NOTHING COMPUTED, and this is the entry to read if only one is read. The roster laid thirteen item ids beside twelve alphabetically sorted county names, each list ordered on its own key, and a reader met a ruled two column table asserting pairings no code had produced. Four rows were false against this run's own claims and the thirteenth orphaned. Two of three judges found it independently. compute.py now emits ask_pairs, one row per item read off that item's own geography. A TABLE IS A CLAIM ABOUT A JOIN, and a join is computed or it is not printed.

Frame 4's dek reversed the actors, reading as though the city or county did the asking when every claim has the county as the body BEING asked. The run's own caption said it the right way round on the same post. Rewritten to match.

entries.register: the inside of an optical instrument and the pedestrian lane it was pointed down, at an international bridge over the Rio Grande after dark. Flocked baffle black, hardcoat anodised housing, coated glass, poured concrete, hot dip galvanized steel, die-cut charcoal foam and river silt.
structural_laws: THE LIGHT HAS TWO OWNERS AND THEY NEVER TRADE ROLES. High pressure sodium is the bridge's own light, ambient, warm, wide and low. 4000K LED is what the test brought, directional, cool, narrow and high. No object in nine frames takes both as its key. Frame 5 declares neither and that is its argument. Two of three treatment directors wrote this law independently without seeing each other, which is the strongest signal that room has produced.

NO FACE, NO BODY, NO PERSON, NO UNIFORM AND NO VEHICLE in nine frames. A deck about facial capture that draws a face has invented the one thing the record does not publish. Movement appears once, on frame 5, as the machine's own record of it.

FILLED MEANS THE ACCOUNT STATES IT. CUT AND EMPTY MEANS IT DOES NOT. Absence is a lit slot with a lip, a side wall and a floor, never a black rectangle, because deck 9 recorded what a black field costs here: it reads as a REDACTION, which says something was removed when the record says nothing was ever stated.
NO RATIO IS DRAWABLE. Six companies demonstrated and three solutions carried forward are counts of different things, so frame 3 puts a hard break at the element line and they never share a scale.

The only dated thing this deck holds is a September 8th briefing on a DIFFERENT program in a different city, and giving it the reserved colour would be the drawing asserting it is a door onto the Progreso test when frame 9's copy and its geometry both say plainly that it is not. One treatment director proposed spending it and another argued it down.

A standing eye height one point corridor off centre, straight up a mast at eighty eight degrees with no ground plane, a dead flat orthographic optical layout, a one point corridor with the vanishing point dead centre, a macro square on at one to one at the image plane, a plan oblique at forty five degrees down two lanes, a shallow three quarter across a machined register, near frontal twelve degrees off axis into a die cut case, and a two point oblique into a sealed housing.

value.note: THE FIRST RENDER MEASURED 6.3 AGAINST A PLAN OF 24, with eight of nine frames between 4.5 and 10.1. That is not dark, it is unlit, and the cause was the same on every frame: each had LIGHTS and no AMBIENT. Every ground, every scrim and the type sitting on them moved, in two passes, and the second pass gave the arc back its shape after the first one flattened the deck into a 13.7 to 17.2 plateau. The shipped figure is the closest any deck here has come to its own plan.

entries.light_decks_used: NONE. Deck median measures well under the 60 threshold, which is the variety debt deck 14 recorded after breaching the cap.
avoid_next: EIGHT OF NINE FRAMES RUN ONE TYPE SKELETON, masthead top left, Fraunces hook, dek beneath, art in the lower half, footer row. Deck 14 avoid_next named seven of nine and asked for better and this deck shipped nine of nine until round 3, when frame 4 moved its names ABOVE the drawing onto inverted light plates. One frame is not the three that were owed. The drawings rotate and the layout still does not. THE NEXT DECK MOVES THE TYPE ON AT LEAST THREE FRAMES, and it plans that in the storyboard rather than repairing it in round 3.

FRAMES 1 AND 4 WERE ONE COMPOSITION TWICE FOR THREE ROUNDS, the closest pair at 0.746 source similarity, both one point corridors with flanking uprights, floor in the bottom half and type in the top third. Two rebuilds moved the geometry and the floor and neither fixed the construction, because the CAMERA was the thing being repeated. The third rebuild changed the camera to a flat elevation and the pair separated. A deck may not spend the same camera class on its cover and on its fulcrum, and the cheapest place to catch that is the storyboard, where nine cameras are declared and nobody compares them.

THE ARGUMENT IS DELEGATED TO MONO LABEL CHIPS on frames 6, 7, 8 and 9, which is what deck 13 was marked down for. Frame 4 carries the same primitive INVERTED, light plate and dark ink, which broke the five-of-nine repeat a round 3 judge counted and does not answer the underlying note. Four frames still hand a chip the job the drawing should do.

SPEND THE INVENTION ON THE FRAMES THE ARGUMENT ENDS ON. Deck 13 asked for this, deck 14 repeated it, and this is the third consecutive deck whose thinnest frames are the fulcrum, the turn and the close.

entries.register: a magnetics assay bench in a dark room at night, under one warm inspection lamp that is never in frame. Oiled hard maple, sintered magnet fracture faces, nickel plating, copper winding under varnish, neodymium oxide powder, brass wire, accession tag stock, and one printed page on ochre survey stock.
structural_laws: LILAC IS THE IMPORTED THING. neodymia appears only where a frame draws rare earth material or the incumbent magnet. Frames 1, 2 and 3 carry it. Frames 6, 7, 8 and 9 carry none, so the colour tracks the imported material out of the deck as the deck moves from the dependency to the search. IT DOES NOT ARGUE THAT THE DEPENDENCY IS DESIGNED OUT, and the first wording of this law said it did. No claim in the file says the project leaves rare earths behind, a scorer hard failed slide 6's dek for saying it, and boride and carbide are anion classes while rare earth is a cation class, so the project's own name excludes nothing. A ledger field is memory, so a refuted reading left in one becomes the next run's premise.

SEATED MEANS MADE. CUT MEANS IMAGINED. A body with a two-part contact shadow is something the record says exists. A cavity is something the record only names. Never a black rectangle, which reads as a redaction. This law is what caught the close: the empty bench had to be LIT for its emptiness to be a measurement rather than an unrendered frame.
NOTHING IS COUNTABLE EXCEPT WHAT A CLAIM COUNTS. No claim gives the size of the candidate space, so frame 7's field runs off all four edges with no boundary and no total.

NO QUANTITY IS DRAWN AS A LENGTH. The import shares are drawn as AREA in true plan. THE POSITION HALF OF THIS LAW WAS MISSING AND THE FRAME BROKE IT: frame 8 put $2.9 million high and $2.88 million low with one continuous wire between them, which is a two point slope built out of props, and every acceptance item on that dossier passed because the list checked size, fill, lighting and the absence of a drawn bar and never checked POSITION.
THE TWO AWARD FIGURES ARE IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION, asserted by frame 8's own script, and the HIGHER tag carries the SMALLER figure so the pair cannot be read as ascending.

entries.red_note: UNSPENT, and the argument is the record's rather than the drawing's. No claim in this file carries a comment window, a hearing or any dated door a reader can act on. --flag-red is for exactly that and nothing else, so no frame carries it and no frame carries a date. texan_check reports deadline NO and next step NO, and both are the record's state.
entries.camera: nine classes, no class twice. True orthographic plan straight down with no horizon, plan oblique at forty five degrees down, a lightless micrograph field with no ground and no cast, a low three quarter on a solid, flat copy square to a page at full bleed, near frontal at ten degrees onto a flat face, a distant orthographic elevation along one long axis, near frontal at ten degrees off axis, and a grazing eye at eight degrees across the bench. The pair the plan worried about was 4 and 6, held apart by solid against flat face.

value.note: THE ARC ABOVE IS A REWRITE AND THE FRAMES WERE REDRAWN FIRST. Both happened and the order matters. The plan read 34, 22, 12, 38, 78, 30, 20, 33, 44 and the first build measured 6.2, 6.2, 8.4, 7.1, 75.9, 28.1, 4.4, 8.2, 3.1, a median of 7.1 against a plan of 33. The ambient floor on six frames went from 6 to 8 up to 25 to 52 and the lamp reach on the close widened by half. Then the arc was rewritten, because a median of 34 means half the pixels of a frame sit at mid grey, which is not a room with one inspection lamp in it. THE SHAPE WAS THE PART THAT MATTERED. The close was the DARKEST frame at 3.1 and it is now 25.9, the third brightest and a real climb out of frame 8.

entries.light_decks_used: NONE. Deck median 16.4, well under the 60 threshold. It is the SECOND DARKEST deck this project has shipped and it sits beside the 15.6, so it does not fill a band the ledger has never seen, which is what the first plan claimed for 33.
avoid_next: SIX TYPE MOVES WERE PLANNED AND THAT DEBT IS PAID. Deck 15's avoid_next asked for a layout that rotates rather than nine frames of one skeleton, and this deck planned six moves in the storyboard rather than repairing one in round 3: the hook to the bottom on 3, the whole type system inverting on 5, the type BECOMING the object on 6, the hook small and low right on 7, tags at opposite corners on 8, and the hook hard left off the patch on 9. THE NEXT DECK OWES SOMETHING ELSE, and the thing it owes is a CLOSE THAT GIVES A READER A DOOR. Three decks running have ended on an absence, and this one could not do otherwise because the record carries no dated anything, but a fourth would be a house style nobody chose.

AN ACCEPTANCE LIST THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A TEST, and this deck shipped two. Frame 8's list checked size, fill, lighting, type and the absence of a drawn bar and never checked POSITION, so the frame drew a slope chart out of props with full marks. Frame 9's absence item was adjudicated by a probe computed from dust counts alone, blind to the wood lift, so it would have reported true on a patch painted white. Both now carry an item that names the thing that actually went wrong. The next run should write at least one MEASURED item per frame at plan time: plan_render_check reported 8 of 61 acceptance items machine checkable here and every one of those eight was written after a critic found the defect.

THE BENCH GRAIN RUNS HORIZONTALLY AND TYPE SITS ON IT. Raising the ambient floor to reach the planned value turned the rake into rules through an 82px serif and a mono list, which the engine calls a strikethrough. A knockout under the line is the answer and flattening the grain is not, but the next dark deck should plan where its type sits BEFORE it plans how much the ground is worked.
